copies.headline: Kaleb's Skill Positions Forgot To Show Up
copies.body:
The running backs ended this before noon. James Cook III and Rhamondre Stevenson put up 40.3 for Noah; Ashton Jeanty and RJ Harvey managed 11.4 for Kaleb, with Harvey contributing 0.7 against an 11.3 projection. That's a 28.9-point hole at one position, and Kaleb never got near it because Carnell Tate (1.6 on 13.5) and Harold Fannin Jr. (1.4 on 12.0) whiffed too. Jordan Addison in the flex scored nothing at all while Keenan Allen's 9.5 sat on the bench.
Noah got 39.5 from Drake Maye, 23.4 from Garrett Wilson and 21.3 from kicker Spencer Shrader, which covered the Cowboys D/ST going negative two with the Browns scoring 11.0 behind them. We had Noah by eight; the actual margin was 55.6, which is less a prediction than a direction.
Noah's 141.3 is a season high and a reminder of what he does in the second half of years. Kaleb drops to 3-2 and was already running +1.1 wins hot — this is the regression arriving, invoice attached.

copies.headline: John's Tight Ends Buried CJ By Themselves
copies.body:
The tight end spot alone was a 16-point swing, and John didn't even need it. Trey McBride went for 21.6, Brock Bowers added 23.0 out of the flex, and CJ answered with Juwan Johnson's 5.6. John won every position except kicker, which is the fantasy equivalent of losing a game 45-3 and pointing at the punting. Puka Nacua's 37.7 with Matthew Stafford throwing it to him was just the cherry — 172.7 is John's season high and the second-best scoring average in the league finally cashing in.
CJ's problem was the middle of his roster collapsing on schedule. Jonathan Taylor missed projection by 7.8, DK Metcalf missed by 7.0 and got outscored by Ka'imi Fairbairn, and Emeka Egbuka sat on the bench with 17.2. Parker Washington's 30.4 was a lovely thing to waste.
Both sit 3-2, but the underlying numbers don't agree: John's 37-18 all-play says he's been the better team all year, CJ's +0.5 luck says he's been getting away with it. We called John by 13 and he tripled it.

copies.headline: Raiders Defense Hands Isaac Another Loss
copies.body:
The margin was 11.9 and the Raiders D/ST was minus six. That's the recap. Isaac won quarterback, won running back by eight, won wide receiver by 3.6 — won the actual football — and still lost because he started a defense that scored less than nothing while Grant's Bengals banked nine. Fifteen points of swing at the one roster spot nobody wants to think about on Sunday morning.
T.J. Hockenson's 1.7 on a 10.5 projection didn't help, and J.K. Dobbins put up 15.4 in street clothes while Cam Skattebo managed 7.1. Grant hardly earned this either: Tony Pollard, Quinshon Judkins and Amon-Ra St. Brown combined to miss projection by 22, and Christian Watson's 32.3 covered all of it. We picked Isaac by nine, which was right about everything except the kicker-adjacent stuff.
Isaac falls to 2-3 with a 16-39 all-play and 11th-place scoring — the record is generous, not cruel. Grant's 3-2 is built on +1.1 luck wins, which is very Grant.

copies.headline: Adam Wins Every Position Peter Needed
copies.body:
The running backs set the table and the special teams buried it. Bucky Irving went for 31.5 and Adam's backfield cleared Peter's by 19.9, which was already more than Peter could absorb given Brian Robinson Jr. turned 8.1 projected points into 1.6. Then the Jets D/ST put up 18.0 against Washington's 3.0 and Will Reichard outkicked Evan McPherson 16.9 to 6.6 — a 25-point swing from the two roster spots nobody drafts on purpose. Adam won five of seven positional slots decisively. Wide receiver was the only place Peter held serve, and he still lost it by 0.8.
Peter's bench was the real crime scene. Denzel Boston scored 13.6 sitting down while Romeo Doubs mustered 2.6, and Roschon Johnson's 9.0 watched Brian Robinson flatline. Flip both and this is still a loss, just a dignified one. Instead, 95.4 is his season low by thirty points.
Adam is 5-0 with a 49-6 all-play, which is the least lucky undefeated start imaginable. Peter's 4-1 was always flattered by schedule — the all-play says 28-27. We had Adam by 16; he got there four times over.

copies.headline: Jaylen Warren and a Tight End Bury Mitchell
copies.body:
Logan won this at the positions nobody circles. Jaylen Warren's 36.8 and Braelon Allen's 18.6 gave him a 55.4-to-40.7 edge at running back, Isaiah Likely's 32.4 beat Tyler Warren by 11, and Joe Burrow outscored Dak Prescott by 12. That's a 37-point cushion across three spots, which is exactly how you survive a kicker who scored 2.0 and a Bears defense that went negative. Mitchell's Broncos D/ST and Tyler Loop clawed back 27.3 of it combined and it still wasn't close enough.
The misses tell the rest. Logan started Jeremiyah Love for 2.2 against a 14.4 projection while MarShawn Lloyd put up 16.7 on the bench — a swing bigger than the 9.4 margin. Mitchell did worse: Konata Mumpfield's zero with Xavier Hutchinson (10.5) and Courtland Sutton (9.8) sitting there. Jahmyr Gibbs went for 37.7 and got nothing for it.
Both are 1-4 with negative luck, but Logan's 142.3 was his season high and his first win since Week 1. Mr. .500 is going to need a different gear than this.

copies.headline: Leif's Receivers Bury Christian's 1-4 Nightmare
copies.body:
Wide receiver decided this one and it wasn't close. Davante Adams and Mike Evans combined for 48.4 while Christian ran out CeeDee Lamb for 2.9 and got 21.6 from the position total. That's a 26.8-point hole before you touch anything else, and Jason Myers adding 25.0 from the kicker slot is the kind of insult that doesn't even require a defense. Leif's 164.3 is his season high by 42.8 points over anything else he's posted.
Christian's problem wasn't effort, it was collapse. Lamb missed his 19.1 projection by 16.2, Chase Brown managed 7.0 on a 17.4 projection, and Kittle chipped in 7.4. Khalil Shakir sat on the bench with 11.0. Leif started David Montgomery for 1.1 with Kyle Pitts at 15.2 behind him and still won by 61.2.
We picked Christian by 11, which looks worse every time you read the box score. He's 1-4 with the fourth-best scoring average and all-play says he's a top-four team. The Aura Farm is farming something, just not wins.

intro: Five of the six games were decided by at least 55 points, which is less a slate than a series of public executions — Adam's 161.76 on Peter and Leif's 164.30 on Christian were the loudest, with John's 172.72 the week's high-water mark. The only real football happened at the margins: Grant survived Isaac by 11.94, and Logan held off Mitchell 142.30-132.94 in the one matchup where both rosters bothered to show up. If your week came down to a decimal point, congratulations, you were in the minority.
